author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The University of New Hampshire women’s volleyball team lost to unbeaten Yale in straight sets Saturday afternoon at the UConn Volleyball Center in Storrs. Yale won 25-16, 25-21 and 25-14, improving to 5-0 while the Wildcats moved to 7-3.

UNH briefly cut Yale’s first-set lead to three with a four-point run and opened the second set with an 8-6 edge. The Bulldogs answered with six consecutive points and controlled the finish. Yale then built an 8-3 lead early in the third set and closed out the match despite a short Wildcats rally.

Emma Converse and Rachel Grier led New Hampshire with eight kills apiece. Reilly Garrity recorded a collegiate-best 13 assists, Hady Pickard had nine digs and three aces, and Grier contributed five total blocks. Yale finished with a .396 hitting percentage and 47 kills, compared with .149 and 31 kills for UNH. The Wildcats next travel to Clemson, South Carolina, to face Furman on September 18.
dek: Reilly Garrity posted a career-high 13 assists, but the Bulldogs hit .396 and won 25-16, 25-21 and 25-14.
headline: UNH volleyball falls to unbeaten Yale in straight sets
